The Xbox One is in second place, with some 46.000 people playing within the last 24 hours. The numbers on the PC, however, are shockingly low, with only around 9,600 people being logged in during peak hours.

Why bait-and-switch these statistics? It's not a fair comparison to list peak consecutive logins against unique daily logins. Peak concurrent players is a measure of popularity and entertainment. If you have a lot of people playing the game in longer sessions, you will have high peak concurrent users. If people play shorter sessions, your peak concurrent users can go down with the same player pool. Unique daily logins removes the effect of session duration on peak concurrent users, but can be deceptive by weighting a one-match-a-day player equal to a 16-hour-a-day streamer. At least list both statistics for all 3 platforms if you're going to swap from one to another mid-article.
